narr: A shortwave trough and a cold front led to the development of scattered to numerous thunderstorms May 4 and 5. Heavy rain causing flash flooding was the main impact during these days. Unfortunately one flash flood fatality occurred in Johnson County.
ev: Cowhouse Creek at Pidcoke rose 10 feet in 40 minutes between 140 AM and 220 AM.
Dozens of flooded and damaged roads were reported across the county, as well as 10 flooded homes, and 17 water rescues conducted by the local fire department and TX Task Force One.
Pecan Bayou at Mullin rose 13 feet between 820 and 920 PM CDT.
A trained spotter reported flooded and impassable low water crossings near and north of Keene.
A public report indicated a flooded home with several inches of water in the yard in Rising Star, TX.

A vehicle occupied by two adults and one 5 year old boy was stranded in swift water off of CR 528. A witness saw the occupants get out of the vehicle and attempt to get to dry ground on foot when all are swept into the flood waters. Responders arrived and began searching for the victims. The adults were found and rescued around 5am and transported to the hospital. The 5 year old victim was found deceased in the water around 7:20am.
Nearly two dozen roads were reported flooded across the city of Dallas.
Law enforcement reported that Trophy Club Bridge had to be closed due to flood waters, and nearby residents were notified about the flooded roads and approaching floodwaters.
A trained spotter reported a vehicle water rescue at the intersection of Shawnee Road and Bells Chapel Road, just south of Red Oak, TX.
Emergency management reported numerous roads were washed out in western Bosque County. Water rescue teams unable to access an emergency scene due to high water.
A trained spotter reported a water rescue on FM 660 just north of Ennis.
Emergency management reported multiple closed roads due to high water near and west of I-35 in Waco, TX.

Fire and rescue reported that TX36 was flooded and impassable at CR 414 and 412 with water rescues occurring SE of Hamilton. Flooded underpasses were also reported in Evant at US281 and US84 resulting in vehicle entrapment. Water over the bridge at CR182 was reported as well.
BNSF Railroad reported on their radio frequency that there was a track washout in the Goldthwaite area.
